Judgment calls: (a) this drafter marks a crossing with a hand-drawn U-shaped detour and leaves real junctions as plain T/cross, so both dips were read as crossovers: at (78-108, 302-312) the ground->resistor-11 wire dives under the x~93 column (so resistor 11 sits between ground and BJT 17's base, and BJT 18/17's collectors reach BJT 19's base untouched), and at (281-304, 374-385) the diode12->diode13 wire dives under the x~292 column (so the diode chain is NOT tied to resistor 9 / V-DC 5). Both were confirmed at 26-28x. (b) The same x~292 column is crossed again at y~430 by the bottom wire with NO detour drawn, so that one is a junction and n15 carries five terminals; this is the least certain call in the file (the corresponding node in the sibling drawing 1166 carries an explicit junction dot, which is why it was read as connected here). (c) Resistor 10 is a series element in the top rail, so the rail left of it is ground and the rail right of it is the +3V node. (d) Emitter arrows read outward-from-bar on all five NPNs (16, 18, 19, 21, 22) and inward-to-bar on all four PNPs (14, 15, 17, 20), matching the class labels; base leads are the perpendicular lead on the opposite side of the bar from C and E in every case. (e) 2-terminal parts indexed as drawn: top-then-bottom for the vertical resistors 8 and 9, left-then-right for resistors 6, 7, 10, 11 and diodes 12 and 13.
